steps.message:
Two files, small blast radius: `index.html:7` has the button, `export.js` contains nothing but that one click handler, and `index.html:8` is the only reference to the script. Nothing else in the repo touches it.

One consequence worth naming before I touch anything: deleting this removes the only way to get report data out of the page — there's no server-side export or download path here, so users lose CSV entirely. You said it's unused, so I'll assume that's intended.

That leaves one real decision:

questions.question: Removing the handler empties export.js completely. How far should the deletion go?

options.label: Delete the file too (Recommended)
options.description: Remove the button from index.html, delete export.js, and drop the <script src="export.js"> tag. Leaves no dead file or 404-ing script reference.

options.label: Button + handler only
options.description: Remove the button and the handler body, but keep export.js (empty) and its <script> tag in place.

steps.message:
Done. The CSV export is gone:

- `export.js` deleted (the whole file was just the one click handler)
- `index.html` — removed the `<button id="export-csv">` and the `<script src="export.js">` tag

No other references remained, so nothing is left pointing at a missing file. The page still renders the report table; it just has no export affordance now. Changes are uncommitted — let me know if you want them committed.
